title: Regional brain structural changes during the transition from acute to chronic neuropathic pain: a longitudinal study in a rat model of orofacial pain.
abstract: Brain imaging studies have identified structural alterations in individuals with chronic neuropathic pain, particularly in regions involved in sensory, emotional, and cognitive processing. However, most studies remain cross-sectional, leaving the temporal progression of these changes during pain chronification unclear. This gap is critical, as both neural and non-neural cells undergo dynamic changes during pain chronification. The primary aim of this study was to track longitudinally, regional brain volume and density changes before and after induction of orofacial neuropathic pain in male rats, using a chronic constriction injury of the infraorbital nerve (ION-CCI). This model enables assessment of changes in the spinal trigeminal nucleus (SpVn). T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging scans were acquired 7-days prior to injury and then at +2, +7, +14, and +28 days, in ION-CCI (n=11), sham-injured (n=6), and naïve (n=8) groups. Voxel-based and deformation-based morphometry were used to identify early- and late-onset density and volumetric changes, respectively. Early after injury, transient, bidirectional volume and/or density changes in the ipsilateral primary somatosensory cortex (S1), contralateral SpVn, and bilateral dorsomedial periaqueductal grey, ipsilateral retrosplenial and contralateral prelimbic cortices, were observed. In contrast, late-onset changes were more widespread, with volume increases observed bilaterally in the SpVn pars interpolaris (SpVo), in the ipsilateral dorsomedial SpVn (SpVdm), bilateral lateral hypothalamus, and contralateral amygdalo-hippocampal complex, and volume decreases in contralateral retrosplenial, prelimbic, and bilateral S1 cortices. These findings reveal early dynamic reorganisation of sensory and sensory-modulatory brain regions, followed by sustained structural alterations across trigeminal brainstem nuclei, limbic-hypothalamic systems, and higher-order cortical networks. Significance Statement Chronic neuropathic pain is associated with structural brain changes, but cross-sectional human studies cannot determine when these alterations emerge, particularly at the primary afferent synapse. Using longitudinal magnetic resonance imaging in a rat model of trigeminal neuropathic pain, we mapped the temporal changes in brain anatomy from pre-injury through pain chronification. We identified an early, transient reorganisation in sensory and modulatory regions, followed by widespread, sustained structural changes in trigeminal brainstem nuclei, including the spinal trigeminal nucleus, limbic-hypothalamic systems, and higher-order cortical networks. These findings provide the first temporal blueprint of brain reorganisation during the transition to chronic orofacial neuropathic pain and establish a mechanistic foundation for identifying early biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

title: Association between urinary NNAL concentrations and osteoarthritis: Evidence from NHANES 2007-2012.
abstract: Introduction Osteoarthritis (OA) is the most prevalent degenerative joint disorder globally, yet the impact of smoking on its development remains contentious. The compound 4-(methylnitrosamino)-1-(3-pyridyl)-1-butanol (NNAL), a principal metabolite of the tobacco-specific nitrosamine 4-(methylnitrosamino)-1-(3-pyridyl)-1-butanone (NNK), is a well-recognized biomarker for smoking exposure. This study aimed to use urinary NNAL as a biomarker to evaluate the association between tobacco exposure and OA. Methods This study was a secondary cross-sectional analysis of pooled data from the 2007-2012 cycles of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), including 10848 adults. OA was assessed using self-reported physician diagnosis and radiographic examination, with a Kellgren-Lawrence grade ≥2 indicating radiographic OA; urinary NNAL concentration was used as the biomarker of tobacco exposure. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression analysis and subgroup analyses were performed after adjusting for confounding factors. Results Elevated urinary NNAL concentrations were positively associated with greater odds of OA. In the fully adjusted model, urinary NNAL concentrations >0.077925 ng/mL were associated with greater odds of OA (adjusted odds ratio, AOR=1.55; 95% CI: 1.36-1.76). Evidence of interaction was observed for age (p for interaction <0.001), but not for sex (p=0.231) or BMI (p=0.127). Among adults aged <60 years, the AOR for the highest versus lowest NNAL category was 1.69 (95% CI: 1.46-1.95), whereas the corresponding AOR was 0.98 (95% CI: 0.82-1.17) among adults aged ≥60 years. Conclusions Higher urinary NNAL was associated with an increased likelihood of OA, with more prominent effects observed in middle-aged adults. Given the cross-sectional design, temporality and causality cannot be established, and the potential association requires confirmation in longitudinal and mechanistic studies.

title: A Case Report of Late Infantile Krabbe Disease: Expanding the Genotype-Phenotype Correlation and Autopsy Findings
abstract: Krabbe disease (KD) is an autosomal recessive neurodegenerative lysosomal disease typically caused by pathogenic variants in GALC, which encodes for the lysosomal galactosylceramidase enzyme. Age of onset is variable, with earlier symptom onset conferring a more severe, and ultimately fatal, disease course. We present a case of an 18-month-old previously healthy female diagnosed with late-infantile KD following a 3-month period of psychomotor regression and irritability. Clinical features included severe axial hypotonia with lower extremity spasticity and hyperreflexia. Whole genome sequencing disclosed a complex GALC genotype including two likely pathogenic variants, p.(Gly284Ser) and p.(Tyr314del), which had not been observed in compound heterozygosity prior. Magnetic resonance imaging displayed symmetric T2 hyperintensity of the central-parietal white matter. The patient ultimately died 6 months after diagnosis from rapidly progressing neurological deterioration. There was significant atrophy on neuropathologic examination, with diffuse globoid cell infiltrate at the supratentorial and infratentorial white matter with relative sparing of the frontal lobe on light microscopy. This patient’s novel genotype, imaging and pathologic findings expand our understanding of the phenotype-genotype correlation in individuals with KD.

title: XAI-AttnFusionNet+: Explainable Multimodal Deep Learning Framework for Early Screening of Pediatric Language Impairment Using rs-fMRI with Hierarchical Attention Fusion
abstract: Pediatric Language Impairment requires timely and consistent screening to enable early intervention and to improve long-term developmental outcomes. Nevertheless, current methods struggle to extract clinically relevant biomarkers from high-dimensional and heterogeneous neuroimaging data, particularly when multimodal analyses and interpretable modeling are not involved. To address these limitations, this paper presents XAI-AttnFusionNet+, an explainable multimodal deep learning model for early-stage Language Impairment screening with early childhood resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI). The proposed model integrates spatial patterns of brain activation, dynamic functional connectivity, and clinical phenotypic characteristics through a hierarchical attention-based fusion mechanism enabling adaptive modality weighting and improved representation learning. To enhance transparency and clinical interpretability, post hoc explainability methods, such as attention visualization, Grad-CAM, and SHAP, were employed to identify discriminative brain regions and feature contributions. The framework was evaluated on a multicenter pediatric cohort of 255 subjects based on ABIDE II using a Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) validation protocol and further evaluated for cross-dataset generalization using ABIDE I. In the absence of Language Impairment annotations, proxy labels were constructed based on phenotypic language indicators. The performance of XAI-AttnFusionNet+ with an accuracy of 93.3% and an AUC of 0.968 outperforms the traditional unimodal baseline models and demonstrates strong cross-site generalization. The results indicate the potential of the proposed framework as a neuroimaging-based approach for early detection of Language Impairment risk. However, its deployment in real-world settings requires further validation using clinically annotated datasets.

title: Diagnostic Performance and Clinical Outcomes of Intraoperative Neuromonitoring in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis: A Comprehensive Analysis of 5,206 Patients.
abstract: Background Curve-specific risk factors for intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) alerts during surgery for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) remain unclear. Methods We identified 5,206 patients with AIS who underwent spinal fusion with multimodal IONM from a prospective database. Alerts were defined as ≥50% amplitude decrease in somatosensory evoked potentials (SSEPs) and/or transcranial motor evoked potentials (TcMEPs), or >10% SSEP latency increase. Demographics, radiographic parameters, surgical variables, triggering events, interventions, and outcomes were compared between the 252 patients with and 4,954 without an alert. Results IONM alerts occurred in 5% of patients. Alert rates varied by Lenke classification, with Type-4 curves demonstrating the highest risk (8%; relative risk [RR] = 1.61, 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.15 to 2.24) and Type 5 demonstrating the lowest risk (2%; RR = 0.45, 95% CI, 0.25 to 0.82). Patients with an alert had a larger mean preoperative major Cobb angle (66.7° ± 15.0° versus 56.1° ± 12.1°, p < 0.001) and more frequent use of Ponte osteotomies (79% versus 66%, p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis demonstrated the major Cobb angle to be the leading independent risk factor for alerts (p < 0.001). Hypotension was the leading triggering event (23%), and raising blood pressure was the most common intervention overall (52%). Neurologic deficits occurred in 4% of patients with an alert versus <1% of those without an alert (p < 0.001). Only 12 patients (<1%) experienced neurologic deficits, with 2 having permanent deficits. At 2-year follow-up, the major Cobb angle correction did not differ significantly between the groups with and without alerts, alert status did not independently affect correction (p = 0.058), and the groups achieved similar outcomes (73% versus 71% correction, respectively). Conclusions IONM alerts occurred in 5% of patients with AIS and were independently associated with a larger major Cobb angle. Fewer than 1% of patients sustained a permanent neurologic injury, and alerts did not appear to compromise 2-year correction. Level of evidence Prognostic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

Alert rates varied by Lenke classification, with Type-4 curves demonstrating the highest risk (8%; relative risk [RR] = 1.61, 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.15 to 2.24) and Type 5 demonstrating the lowest risk (2%; RR = 0.45, 95% CI, 0.25 to 0.82). Patients with an alert had a larger mean preoperative major Cobb angle (66.7° ± 15.0° versus 56.1° ± 12.1°, p < 0.001) and more frequent use of Ponte osteotomies (79% versus 66%, p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis demonstrated the major Cobb angle to be the leading independent risk factor for alerts (p < 0.001). Hypotension was the leading triggering event (23%), and raising blood pressure was the most common intervention overall (52%). Neurologic deficits occurred in 4% of patients with an alert versus <1% of those without an alert (p < 0.001). Only 12 patients (<1%) experienced neurologic deficits, with 2 having permanent deficits. At 2-year follow-up, the major Cobb angle correction did not differ significantly between the groups with and without alerts, alert status did not independently affect correction (p = 0.058), and the groups achieved similar outcomes (73% versus 71% correction, respectively).

Conclusions

IONM alerts occurred in 5% of patients with AIS and were independently associated with a larger major Cobb angle. Fewer than 1% of patients sustained a permanent neurologic injury, and alerts did not appear to compromise 2-year correction.

Prognostic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Extra-Articular Malunions and Nonunions of the Scapular Body and Neck: A Comparison of Functional Outcomes Before and After Reconstruction.
abstract: Background Malunions and nonunions of scapular neck and body fractures can cause considerable pain and disability. This study reports outcomes regarding functional measures, range of motion, and strength before and after reconstruction. Methods This retrospective case series at a Level-1 trauma center between 2003 and 2024 identified 50 consecutive patients (mean age, 50.3 years; 82% male; 80% White) with symptomatic malunion or nonunion of a scapular neck and/or body fracture who were referred to a single surgeon. Medial-lateral displacement and angular deformity were corrected through surgical reconstruction and malunion osteotomy. The Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand (DASH) score, range of motion, strength, and postoperative procedures requiring a return to the operating room were recorded. Results Fifty patients were included in the study; 5 patients were lost to follow-up before 12 months, leaving 45 patients (40 with malunion and 5 with nonunion) with >1-year outcomes. Eleven patients underwent reconstruction between 6 weeks and 3 months after injury because of the severity of the injury, their symptoms, and/or the necessity of an osteotomy. The median time from injury to reconstruction was 10 months (interquartile range [IQR] width, 16 months), and the median follow-up was 28.9 months (IQR width, 23.2 months). All patients achieved radiographic evidence of union. No intraoperative complications occurred. There was a mean 30.7-point improvement between the preoperative and final postoperative DASH scores (p < 0.001). The mean postoperative DASH score was 14.1 in patients who underwent reconstruction between 6 weeks and 3 months and was 23.2 in those who underwent reconstruction after 3 months. Forward flexion and abduction demonstrated significant increases in both range of motion and strength from preoperatively to postoperatively. External rotation range of motion and strength showed no significant increases. Subsequent procedures were performed in 12 patients: 8 patients underwent symptomatic implant removal (1 also underwent concurrent manipulation under anesthesia), 1 patient underwent open reduction and internal fixation for a new fracture, 2 patients underwent implant revision (1 also underwent concurrent manipulation under anesthesia), and 1 patient underwent manipulation under anesthesia for shoulder contracture. Conclusions Extra-articular scapular malunions and nonunions can be associated with considerable pain and disability. Deformity correction improved range of motion and strength and reduced disability in this cohort. A principled reconstruction can be successful in addressing the sequelae of displaced scapular fractures. Level of evidence Therapeutic Level IV. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Hearing impairment is associated with impaired glymphatic function in middle- and older-aged adults: evidence from DTI-ALPS imaging
abstract: Abstract Hearing impairment is a common age-related sensory disorder and has been increasingly linked to central nervous system changes beyond peripheral auditory dysfunction. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between hearing impairment and glymphatic system function using the diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index, and to explore its potential as an imaging biomarker in middle- and older-aged adults. A total of 131 participants aged 45–80 years were enrolled, including 71 individuals with normal hearing and 60 with hearing impairment defined by pure-tone average thresholds ≥ 25 dB HL. All participants underwent brain MRI with diffusion tensor imaging, and glymphatic function was evaluated using the DTI-ALPS index. Cognitive function was assessed using the Mini-Mental State Examination and Montreal Cognitive Assessment. Associations between pure-tone average and DTI-ALPS indices were examined using Spearman correlation analysis. Logistic regression models were applied to identify independent factors associated with hearing impairment, and receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to evaluate diagnostic performance. Participants with hearing impairment were older, more frequently male, and exhibited lower MoCA scores compared with controls. Global and regional DTI-ALPS indices were significantly reduced in the hearing impairment group and were inversely correlated with hearing thresholds. In multivariate analysis, both older age and lower DTI-ALPS index remained independently associated with hearing impairment. The combined model incorporating age and DTI-ALPS achieved the best discriminative performance. These findings suggest that hearing impairment is independently associated with reduced glymphatic system function, and that the DTI-ALPS index, particularly when combined with age, may serve as a promising imaging biomarker for age-related hearing decline.

title: Longitudinal CT-Based Assessment of Early Bone–Implant Interface Changes after 3D-Printed Titanium Limb-Salvage Reconstruction: A Finite Element and Radiomics Proof-of-Concept Study
abstract: Abstract Background Early assessment of bone–implant interface integration after 3D-printed titanium reconstruction remains challenging. This study aimed to explore the feasibility of a longitudinal CT-based framework integrating finite element analysis and radiomics for postoperative assessment of early interface changes after limb-salvage reconstruction. Methods A patient who underwent bone tumor resection followed by reconstruction with a patient-specific 3D-printed titanium prosthesis was retrospectively included. Serial thin-slice CT scans obtained at 1, 2, 3, and 4 months postoperatively were used for three-dimensional reconstruction, longitudinal rigid registration, finite element analysis under representative loading conditions, and CT radiomic feature extraction. Biomechanical indicators and radiomic features were analyzed descriptively across follow-up time points. Results Longitudinal finite element analysis showed a gradual decrease in total deformation, implant von Mises stress, and talar surface peak equivalent stress across the early postoperative period. CT radiomic analysis showed increasing first-order mean values, decreasing GLDM dependence non-uniformity, and increasing GLCM inverse variance. Exploratory correlation analysis suggested concordant temporal changes between selected biomechanical indicators and radiomic features. Conclusions This proof-of-concept study demonstrates the feasibility of integrating longitudinal CT radiomics with finite element analysis to assess early bone–implant interface changes after 3D-printed titanium limb-salvage reconstruction. This framework may provide a noninvasive approach for postoperative monitoring and implant-interface assessment, although validation in larger cohorts is required.

title: Automated Pipeline for Prediction of Spontaneous Paediatric Intracerebral Haemorrhage Outcome Based on CT Images
abstract: Abstract Purpose This study aimed to develop a machine learning model for predicting the outcome of spontaneous paediatric intracerebral haemorrhage (sICH) by leveraging automatically segmented volumes of total brain (TB), intraparenchymal haemorrhage (IPH), intraventricular haemorrhage (IVH), and perihaematomal oedema (PHE) from cranial CT images in conjunction with clinical data. Methods A retrospective, bi-center study of sICH patients was conducted. The Fudan University Children's Hospital (FUCH) cohort was split 7:3 for training/internal testing, while the Zhejiang University Children’s Hospital (ZUCH) cohort served for external validation. Automated and manual segmentation extracted regions of interest (TB, IPH, IVH, PHE), from which quantitative hematoma volume parameters (e.g., IPH/total brain volume ratio) were derived. Three models were developed: a hematoma location/complication (HLC) model, a hematoma quantification (HQ) model, and a combined model integrating both feature sets. Classifiers (logistic regression, support vector machine, decision tree) were trained with 10-fold cross-validation. Performance was evaluated via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) and decision curve analysis (DCA) on both test sets; SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) interpreted the combined model. Results Among 147 patients (median age 6.6 years ± 4.28 [SD]; 84 (57.1%) males), 49 (33.3%) had poor outcomes (mRS ≥ 3). Automatic segmentation showed high consistency with radiologists (Dice: IPH 0.837, IVH 0.745; Lin coefficient > 0.8). The combined model outperformed the HLC and HQ models, achieving AUCs of 0.798 (internal) and 0.822 (external). DCA indicated greater clinical net benefit for the combined model across thresholds of 0.10–0.59. The pipeline completed automated segmentation and volume analysis per patient in under 17 seconds. Conclusion The automated pipeline for spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage based on CT images can objectively and accurately predict the outcome of intracerebral haemorrhage in children.

title: A Rare Case of Breast Cancer with Nasopharyngeal Metastasis: A Case Report and Literature Review
abstract: Abstract Although nasopharyngeal metastatic tumors are rare, breast cancer metastasis is uncommon. This report describes a 43-year-old female who developed a nasopharyngeal metastatic lesion after several cycles of breast cancer treatment. She was diagnosed with left breast infiltrating ductal carcinoma (pT2N0M0, Stage II) eight years ago. However, the patient did not undergo standard postoperative adjuvant therapy. She also developed axillary lymph node metastasis during the course of the illness. Although she underwent several systemic treatment cycles, imaging revealed aberrant nasopharyngeal hypertrophy. Endoscopy revealed a single elevated mass within the eustachian tube of the right pharyngeal recess. A pathological biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of breast cancer metastasis. Partial lesion response was achieved on MRIs after administering local intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT, 66 Gy in 33 fractions). The present case underscores the need to be vigilant for atypical metastases during oncological follow-up, as well as the effectiveness of multidisciplinary cooperation in diagnosing and treating such tumors.

title: Clinically Diagnosed Diamond-Blackfan Anemia with Negative Whole Exome Sequencing in an Infant with Crossed Renal Ectopia: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA) is a rare congenital bone marrow failure syndrome presenting with early-onset anemia and reticulocytopenia. Approximately 30–40% of clinically typical cases remain genetically unresolved on exome sequencing, and a diagnosis can still be established on clinical and morphological grounds when the phenotype is characteristic. Case presentation: We report an 80-day-old female infant of non-consanguineous parentage who presented with pallor, poor feeding, and severe transfusion-dependent anemia with reticulocytopenia since birth. Bone marrow examination showed a normocellular marrow with marked erythroid paucity and an elevated myeloid-to-erythroid ratio, with adequate megakaryocytes and no fibrosis or malignancy. Whole exome sequencing targeting RPS19, GATA1, and TSR2 was non-diagnostic, revealing only a heterozygous variant of uncertain significance in KMT2D. Contrast-enhanced CT urography incidentally identified a non-fused crossed ectopic left kidney. Alternative nutritional, infectious, and inherited marrow failure causes were excluded, and a clinical diagnosis of DBA was made. The infant was managed with packed red blood cell transfusion and supportive care. Conclusion This case illustrates that DBA can be diagnosed on clinical and morphological grounds despite a negative exome sequencing result, and describes non-fused crossed renal ectopia as an anomaly not previously reported in association with DBA, broadening the recognized spectrum of congenital anomalies in this disorder.

title: Acute shoulder gouty arthritis complicated by partial rotator cuff tear misdiagnosed as calcific tendinitis: a case report and literature review
abstract: Abstract Background Acute shoulder gout concurrent with rotator cuff injury is extremely rare in clinical practice. This disease presents non-specific clinical manifestations and conventional imaging features, resulting in a high misdiagnosis rate. Relevant clinical studies remain limited. We report a typical case herein, summarize the core causes of misdiagnosis, and refine standardized diagnostic and therapeutic principles, aiming to provide evidence-based references for precise clinical diagnosis and management of similar conditions. Case presentation A 52-year-old male patient presented with abrupt severe right shoulder pain lasting 2 days. He had a long-standing history of gout involving the first metatarsophalangeal and knee joints with poorly controlled serum uric acid. Laboratory tests revealed significantly elevated serum uric acid and systemic inflammatory markers. Preoperative computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) initially indicated calcific tendinitis, and symptoms failed to resolve after routine conservative treatment. Arthroscopic exploration revealed extensive chalky white monosodium urate (MSU) crystal deposition on the acromial and tendinous surfaces, combined with a partial supraspinatus tendon tear. Intraoperative synovectomy, thorough crystal debridement, and rotator cuff repair were performed. Postoperative histopathology confirmed the diagnosis of shoulder gouty arthritis. Standard long-term urate-lowering therapy was administered postoperatively, achieving significant pain relief. At the 3-month follow-up, serum uric acid was stably controlled, and full shoulder function was recovered. Conclusion Acute shoulder gout combined with rotator cuff tear is a rare clinical entity that is frequently misdiagnosed as calcific tendinitis. High clinical suspicion for shoulder gout should be maintained in patients with hyperuricemia or a gout history presenting with acute severe shoulder pain. Arthroscopic debridement combined with rotator cuff repair, followed by standardized long-term urate-lowering therapy and adjuvant traditional Chinese medicine intervention, can substantially improve long-term clinical outcomes.

title: Imaging-driven early intervention for BAV-IE with atypical symptoms and severe multisystem complications: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is the most prevalent congenital cardiac malformation and confers a markedly elevated risk of infective endocarditis (IE).Severe concurrent complications, including perivalvular abscess, ruptured aortic sinus aneurysm, pseudoaneurysm, and complete atrioventricular block(AVB), rarely coexist in a single patient, and afebrile atypical presentations further delay diagnosis. Cardiac computed tomography angiography (CTA) enables comprehensive preoperative anatomical mapping for complex BAV-IE, yet standardized imaging-driven management experience for this extreme disease spectrum remains scarce. Methods We report a 59-year-old afebrile male patient presenting with 4 months of exertional dyspnea. Preoperative cardiac CTA with 3D volume rendering was performed to delineate valvular, perivalvular, and aortic root lesions.A composite radical Bentall-based surgical procedure was delivered, with postoperative blood culture and 3-year serial echocardiographic follow-up. All imaging data were anonymized for publication. Results CTA confirmed congenital type 0 BAV, IE with perivalvular abscess, 18 mm coronary sinus rupture forming a 5.0×4.5 cm aortic root pseudoaneurysm, and third-degree atrioventricular block.Intraoperative debridement combined with aortic root replacement, multi-valvular repair, and temporary epicardial pacing was completed successfully.Streptococcus mitis was isolated from blood cultures.Over three years of follow-up, the mechanical valve remained functionally stable, graft flow stayed unobstructed, and all clinical symptoms completely resolved. Conclusions Cardiac CTA with 3D visualization provides definitive preoperative anatomical stratification for multi-complicated atypical BAV-IE.Early radical composite surgery guided by comprehensive imaging yields a favorable long-term prognosis, even in elderly afebrile patients with four concurrent severe cardiovascular complications.This case highlights the irreplaceable role of multimodal cardiac imaging in risk stratification and surgical planning for complex BAV-associated endocarditis.

title: Ultrasound guided Glossopharyngeal and Maxillary Nerve Blocks for Perioperative Pain Control in Adenotonsillectomy in Pediatrics: Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Abstract Background: Adeno-tonsillectomy surgery in pediatrics is associated with increased postoperative pain and discomfort, so combined bilateral ultrasound-guided glossopharyngeal nerve ( UGGNB ) and ultrasound-guided maxillary nerve ( UGMNB ) in pediatric patients undergoing adenotonsillectomy surgeries to validate previous findings & to help decrease perioperative opioid consumption and respiratory complications Objective: Efficacy of combined bilateral glossopharyngeal nerve block and bilateral maxillary nerve block on perioperative management of tonsillectomy under general anesthesia provide excellent analgesic profile & significant differences in food intake postoperatively. Methods: 40 Patients was randomly allocated into two groups: Block Group: 20 patients received combined bilateral UGGNB and UGMNB. Conventional Group: 20 patients received IV paracetamol 15mg/kg. Intraoperative hemodynamics were recorded baseline and at 15 minutes intervals. Quality of analgesia was assessed using Wong-Baker FACES scale for children more than 3 years of age up to 8 years of age and VAS score for older children every 30 minutes for 1 hours after recovery from anesthesia in PACU and every 2, 4, 8, 12, and 24 hours postoperative after transferring to the ward. For postoperative pain therapy, if pain scale scores are ≥ 4, first was IV ibuprofen 7.5mg/kg immediately postoperative. Results: -Pain was assessed by VAS or FACES scores, according to patient age, postoperative after 30 min, then at 1, 2, 4, 8, 12 and 24 hours, where group B patients had significantly lower pain scores at all-time points (p≤ 0.043) except after 24 h (p=0.355). -Time to first rescue analgesia was significantly longer in Group B than in Group C (10.9±1.9 h vs. 5.1±2.4 h, p=0.001). -Time to first rescue analgesia was significantly delayed in Group B (P = 0.001). -There was no statistically significant difference in pethidine consumption between the two groups within the first 4 hours or over 24 hours (P=0.171). -Group B patients needed significantly less Paracetamol (70% vs. 100%, p=0.020), yet, with comparable dose to Group C patients (7.1±5.5 vs. 7.8±2.3 ml, p=0.608). Conclusion: Combined bilateral ultrasound-guided glossopharyngeal and maxillary nerve blocks provide superior postoperative analgesia compared to conventional multimodal analgesia with intravenous paracetamol for tonsillectomy patients. The technique resulted in significantly lower pain scores, prolonged time to first rescue analgesia, reduced supplemental analgesic consumption, shorter PACU stay, and higher parent satisfaction, all with an excellent safety profile. Trial Registration: on clinicaltrials.gov, ( NCT07379866) at 24 November 2025.

title: Successful Management of Autoimmune Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis Complicating Rheumatoid Arthritis with Whole-lung Lavage and De-escalation of Anti-rheumatic Therapy: A Report of Two Cases
abstract: Abstract Background Autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (APAP) is characterized by elevated levels of autoantibodies against granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF), resulting in the accumulation of surfactant proteins within the alveoli. Immunosuppressive therapy is generally considered harmful in APAP, but the clinical impact of reducing immunosuppressive therapy on concomitant connective tissue disease remains unclear. Case presentation Case 1: A 69-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in clinical remission on methotrexate, iguratimod, and salazosulfapyridine developed exertional dyspnea. Chest High-resolution computed tomography showed bilateral ground-glass opacities with a crazy-paving appearance, and APAP was diagnosed based on bronchoalveolar lavage findings and elevated serum anti-GM-CSF autoantibody levels. Whole-lung lavage (WLL) resulted in improvement, but APAP recurred one year later and required a second WLL. During APAP management, anti-rheumatic therapy was gradually tapered and discontinued, and she remained free of both APAP recurrence and RA flare for two years after the second WLL. Case 2: A 67-year-old man with RA treated with salazosulfapyridine was found to have bilateral diffuse bilateral ground-grass opacities on routine chest imaging and was subsequently diagnosed with APAP based on a positive serum anti-GM-CSF autoantibody testing. Because he was initially asymptomatic with preserved oxygenation, careful observation was chosen. After disease progression, WLL was performed, followed by gradual tapering of salazosulfapyridine. APAP relapsed three months later and improved after a second WLL, by which time salazosulfapyridine had been discontinued. He has remained free of respiratory symptoms and RA flare without medication for more than five years. Conclusion In selected patients with RA who develop APAP, tapering anti-rheumatic medication may allow APAP to be managed without loss of RA control. These cases suggest a possible immunomodulatory role of anti-GM-CSF autoantibodies and indicate that careful re-evaluation and adjustment of RA treatment after the onset of APAP may help achieve a more favorable balance between APAP control and RA disease activity.

title: Diagnostic Utility of Pentraxin-3 Compared With N-terminal-prohormone of B-Type Natriuretic Peptide (Nt-probnp) and Tumour Necrosis Factor-α (Tnf-α) in Dogs With Degenerative Mitral Valve Disease
abstract: Abstract Pentraxin-3 (PTX3) is a novel biomarker of interest in cardiovascular disease and injury. Despite this, there is limited literature on PTX3 as a veterinary biomarker. Another ubiquitous inflammatory marker, tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), has been studied extensively in dogs with DMVD, with mixed findings. The N-terminal-prohormone of B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is a routinely used biomarker of canine cardiac dysfunction. This study compared the diagnostic utility of PTX3 with TNF-α and NT-proBNP in dogs with DMVD. Serum NT-proBNP, PTX3, and TNF-α were measured in 50 client-owned dogs diagnosed and staged according to the ACVIM stages A-D. Echocardiographic variables, radiographic vertebral heart score (VHS) and vertebral left atrial size (VLAS), systolic blood pressure (SBP), and quality of life (QoL) scores were assessed. The Kruskal-Wallis test was used to compare PTX3, TNF-α, and NT-proBNP levels between different stages of DMVD, and the Jonckheere-Terpstra test assessed whether serum biomarker concentrations showed a significant ordered trend across progressively worsening DMVD across stages. Spearman’s correlation was used to assess the associations between biomarker levels, disease stage, QoL scores, SBP, radiographic, and echocardiographic parameters. Concentration of PTX3 and TNF-α did not differ significantly across DMVD stages, while only NT-proBNP showed significant variation between stages (p = 0.02). Jonckheere-Terpstra trend test revealed a significant ordered trend in serum NT-proBNP (p < 0.01), but not PTX3 and TNF-α across DMVD stages. NT-proBNP correlated significantly with DMVD stage, QoL score, VHS, VLAS, and echocardiographic variables including LVIDdn, LA:Ao (p < 0.01), and EF%, FS% (p = 0.02). NT-proBNP remains a reliable biomarker for diagnosis, disease monitoring, and prognosis assessment in canine DMVD. Future studies employing larger longitudinal cohorts will be essential to better elucidate the role of inflammatory markers in canine heart disease.

title: Attention-Based Deep learning Network for automatic detection of Microsatellite Instability in endoscopy images
abstract: Abstract Background Microsatellite instability (MSI) is a clinically relevant biomarker in colorectal cancer (CRC). In this study, we employed a deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) model to differentiate between MSI and microsatellite-stable (MSS) status using endoscopic images. Methods A pathology-proven dataset was constructed from 986 colonoscopy images of 176 patients with CRC. The images were partitioned into training, validation, and test sets. Attention-based ResNet-50 and MobileNet-V2 DCNN architectures were trained and evaluated for their discriminatory performance. The area under the curve (AUC) was used as the primary performance metric, supplemented by accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and precision. Results In the test cohort, the MobileNet-SE model achieved the best performance, with an AUC of 0.874 (95% CI: 0.852–0.896), a precision of 0.830 (95% CI: 0.787–0.863), a sensitivity of 0.714 (95% CI: 0.670–0.754), a specificity of 0.852 (95% CI: 0.815–0.882), and an accuracy of 0.782 (95% CI: 0.754–0.808). Conclusions These findings underscore the clinical utility of endoscopic images in MSI screening and establish a benchmark for an optimal MSI prediction model.

title: Multidisciplinary decision-making in the management of recurrent glioblastoma - a multi-centre UK questionnaire study
abstract: Abstract Background Recurrent glioblastoma (GB) carries a poor prognosis, with physical and cognitive decline significantly affecting patients’ survival and quality of life. Unlike newly-diagnosed GB, there is a paucity of level 1 evidence to guide management, including uncertainty regarding the clinical efficacy and cost-effectiveness of repeat resection prior to second-line chemotherapy. We surveyed UK neuro-oncology specialists to evaluate decision-making practices regarding recurrent GB management and the clinical features influencing them. Methods Between December 2023 and April 2024, a 35-item questionnaire was distributed to consultant neuro-oncologists and neuro-oncology surgeons. Respondents were presented with seven case vignettes simulating first GB recurrences and asked to select suitable treatments, including their single preferred option. We also explored which factors routinely influenced decision-making and extent of multi-disciplinary team (MDT) involvement. Results Thirty-eight responses came from 23 consultant neuro-oncology surgeons and 15 consultant neuro-oncologists across 22 NHS hospitals (response rate 73%). Only 71% routinely re-discussed first recurrence at MDT meetings, with higher re-presentation rates among surgeons. Use of advanced imaging to confirm recurrence was variable: MRI perfusion (74%), MR spectroscopy (53%) and no routine advanced imaging (24%). Across seven vignettes, repeat resection followed by second-line chemotherapy was favoured in focally-restricted and late recurrences, but rarely considered for deep-seated or multifocal disease. Second-line chemotherapy was deemed feasible in most scenarios. Re-irradiation was rarely selected, except in late recurrence with good performance status. Best supportive care was often identified as feasible alongside active treatments, particularly with poor prognostic indicators. Factors most commonly influencing re-resection decisions included recurrence interval, performance status, anticipated extent of resection, eloquence and number of tumour foci. Conclusions Substantial inter-clinician variability in preferred management suggests a high degree of clinical equipoise. In this context, there is strong support for randomised trials exploring the clinical efficacy of different management options in recurrent GB, including re- resection surgery.

title: Oral lichen planus in a patient with neurofibromatosis type 1: the first biopsy- confirmed case report
abstract: Abstract Oral lichen planus co-occurring with neurofibromatosis type 1 is exceptionally rare. A comprehensive literature search revealed no prior reports of biopsy-confirmed OLP in NF1 patients. This report describes the first such case in a 22-year-old woman with familial NF1 confirmed by whole exome sequencing (pathogenic variant: c.2850 + 1delG). The patient presented with a 6-month history of intermittent burning and discomfort in the buccal mucosa during orthodontic treatment. Clinical examination showed bilateral reticular white striae with erythematous erosions on the buccal mucosa, alongside classic NF1 features including multiple café-au-lait macules and neurofibromas. Differential diagnoses such as lichenoid reaction to amalgam, systemic lupus erythematosus, and drug-induced lichenoid reaction were excluded based on the absence of any amalgam restorations, negative serological tests for autoimmune markers (including ANA and anti-dsDNA), lack of systemic symptoms suggestive of SLE, and no history of medications associated with lichenoid reactions. The diagnosis of erosive OLP was clinicopathologic, supported by histopathology revealing band-like lymphocytic infiltrate, basal keratinocyte necrosis, and Civatte bodies. Treatment included incisional biopsy and topical triamcinolone acetonide 0.1%, resulting in complete resolution of lesions and symptoms within one month. No recurrence was observed during the 6-month follow-up, and orthodontic treatment progressed uneventfully. This case documents the first biopsy-confirmed erosive OLP in an NF1 patient, emphasizing the importance of routine oral screening and multidisciplinary management given the potential risk of malignant transformation in OLP (approximately 1–2%).

title: Neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio and late gadolinium enhancement in clinically suspected myocarditis: a multicentre retrospective study
abstract: Abstract Background Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging identifies myocardial involvement in myocarditis and carries prognostic weight. The neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio (NPAR) combines neutrophil predominance with serum albumin, a negative acute-phase reactant. Whether NPAR is associated with LGE, and whether it adds information to its individual components and to routinely available clinical data, is unknown. Methods This retrospective observational study included 1,055 adults with clinically suspected myocarditis who underwent CMR at seven tertiary cardiovascular centres in Türkiye between October 2022 and September 2025. All studies were reviewed centrally by three cardiovascular radiologists blinded to clinical and laboratory data (Fleiss' κ = 0.83). Variables significant on univariable analysis (p < 0.10) were entered into multivariable logistic regression models, the shape of the association was examined using restricted cubic splines, and the incremental value of NPAR over the clinical and laboratory model was assessed using discrimination and reclassification metrics. Results LGE was present in 285 patients (27.0%). NPAR was higher in the LGE-positive group [1.65 (1.40–1.92) vs. 1.29 (1.02–1.55); p < 0.001]. In the multivariable model, NPAR remained independently associated with LGE positivity (adjusted odds ratio per 1 standard deviation 4.381, 95% confidence interval 3.248–5.907; p < 0.001), and the Nagelkerke R² rose from 0.157 to 0.387. Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a positive association across the observed range with evidence of non-linearity (p = 0.013). Adding NPAR increased the area under the curve of the model from 0.728 (0.687–0.768) to 0.839 (0.806–0.872) (difference 0.111; p < 0.001), with an integrated discrimination improvement of 0.194 (0.133–0.251) and a continuous net reclassification improvement of 0.843 (0.674–1.011), both p < 0.001. As a single marker, NPAR yielded an area under the curve of 0.750 (0.718–0.782) at a cut-off of 1.43, discriminating LGE better than either constituent (both p < 0.0001). Conclusions In clinically suspected myocarditis, NPAR was independently associated with CMR-defined LGE positivity, discriminated LGE better than either of its own components, and provided significant incremental discrimination and reclassification over a clinical and laboratory model. NPAR may serve as a low-cost adjunctive marker where access to CMR is constrained.

title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Shoulder Pseudodislocation Secondary to Calcific Tendinopathy: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Shoulder pseudodislocation is a rare clinical condition. Imaging examination shows displacement of the humeral head relative to the glenoid, while the osseous anatomical alignment of the joint remains intact. This article reports a 52-year-old female patient with a long history of rotator cuff calcific tendinopathy. The patient presented with recurrent chronic dull shoulder pain, recently aggravated pain, and restricted shoulder movement. Shoulder radiography revealed a dislocation-like appearance of the glenohumeral joint, calcified lesions located at the superolateral humeral head, and widening of the glenohumeral joint space. Given the absence of shoulder trauma, immediate manual reduction was not performed. Further multimodal imaging examinations including CT and MRI were completed, and the patient was finally diagnosed with shoulder pseudodislocation secondary to calcific tendinitis. CT demonstrated calcified deposits at the superolateral humeral head, whereas MRI showed supraspinatus tendon injury, extensive periarticular soft tissue edema, and glenohumeral joint capsular effusion. The patient underwent arthroscopic calcified lesion debridement combined with subacromial decompression. Postoperative radiographic reexamination at day 1 and 2 weeks revealed significant reduction of calcified lesions and gradual recovery of the abnormally widened glenohumeral joint space. Postoperative follow-up showed nearly complete relief of shoulder pain, full recovery of shoulder forward flexion, external rotation and abduction, and unremarkable limitation in daily activities. Based on this rare case, the present study aims to summarize the imaging characteristics and diagnostic and therapeutic strategies of shoulder pseudodislocation secondary to calcific tendinitis, to distinguish soft tissue-induced pseudodislocation from traumatic true shoulder dislocation, and to avoid unnecessary closed reduction. This study provides clinical evidence for preoperative imaging evaluation and minimally invasive surgical treatment of similar rare secondary shoulder lesions.

Postoperative follow-up showed nearly complete relief of shoulder pain, full recovery of shoulder forward flexion, external rotation and abduction, and unremarkable limitation in daily activities. Based on this rare case, the present study aims to summarize the imaging characteristics and diagnostic and therapeutic strategies of shoulder pseudodislocation secondary to calcific tendinitis, to distinguish soft tissue-induced pseudodislocation from traumatic true shoulder dislocation, and to avoid unnecessary closed reduction. This study provides clinical evidence for preoperative imaging evaluation and minimally invasive surgical treatment of similar rare secondary shoulder lesions.

title: Clinicopathological Features and Prognosis of Acute Interstitial Nephritis: A Study of 26 Patients
abstract: Abstract Objective : Acute interstitial nephritis (AIN) is an acute kidney injury (AKI) characterized by renal interstitial inflammation and tubular damage. This study aims to clarify its clinical features, etiologies, and prognosis. Methods: Clinical data from 26 AIN patients were retrospectively analyzed, including demographics, manifestations, lab tests, ultrasound, pathology, etiology, and outcomes. Results: Mean age was 54.8 years, with 53.8% aged 51–70 years. Females accounted for 61.5% (M:F=1:1.6). Hypertension (42.3%) and diabetes (19.2%) were common comorbidities. Digestive symptoms (38.5%) were the most frequent presentation. AKI occurred in 88.5%, all stage 3, and 38.5% received short-term hemodialysis. Lab findings showed elevated creatinine, BUN, and uric acid, with mild anemia in some. Renal ultrasound revealed increased cortical echogenicity (42.3%) and cysts (23.0%). Biopsy demonstrated interstitial inflammatory infiltration (mainly lymphocytes) in all cases, and 76.9% had interstitial fibrosis. Drug-related causes accounted for 30.8%, while 30.8% remained unknown. Eighteen patients received glucocorticoids. After 3 months, 22 patients were followed up, with a renal recovery rate of 95.5%. Conclusion: AIN is more common in middle-aged and elderly women, with drugs being a major causative factor. It typically presents as severe AKI. Renal biopsy reveals characteristic interstitial inflammation. With active treatment, the overall prognosis is favorable. Emphasis should be placed on preventing and early identifying drug-induced kidney injury.

title: Natural Language Processing and Large Language Model-Based Automated AO/OTA Classification of Proximal Femoral Fractures: A MIMIC-IV Retrospective Study
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate AO/OTA classification of proximal femoral fractures is a critical step in surgical decision-making and prognostic evaluation; however, the complexity of the classification system and the heterogeneity of terminology in radiology reports pose significant challenges for large-scale, standardized application of the classification. In recent years, with the advancement of AI technologies, large language models (LLMs) equipped with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) capabilities have offered new possibilities for automatically extracting fracture classification information from unstructured radiology reports. Methods This study conducted a retrospective analysis of 23,179 radiology reports from the MIMIC-IV database. Through a multi-stage annotation process involving independent labeling by two orthopedic surgeons and adjudication by a senior expert, a total of 157 acute cases of AO/OTA type 31A (intertrochanteric fractures) and type 31B (femoral neck fractures) were ultimately included. We evaluated three experimental models: zero‑shot prompting, few‑shot learning (5 examples per class), and RAG‑augmented prompting (incorporating a structured AO classification knowledge base). Classification performance was assessed using accuracy, F1‑score, and confusion matrices. All type 31C (femoral head fractures) cases underwent expert re‑adjudication to evaluate annotation quality. Results The RAG‑LLM framework achieved an accuracy of 94.29% (F1 = 94.29%) in distinguishing 31A from 31B fractures on a balanced test set of 70 cases (35 each of 31A and 31B). Zero‑shot prompting attained the same accuracy (94.29%, F1 = 94.28%), while few‑shot learning unexpectedly dropped to 88.57% (F1 = 88.53%). Confusion matrices showed minimal misclassifications: 2/35 cases of 31A were misclassified as 31B, and 2/35 cases of 31B were misclassified as 31A. A key finding was that after expert re‑adjudication of 47 cases initially labeled as 31C, only 6 (12.8%) met the true AO/OTA 31C criteria; the remaining 41 (87.2%) were actually acetabular fractures (AO/OTA type 61) or misclassified 31A/31B cases. The subtype classification for 31B fractures (31B1 vs. 31B2) achieved an accuracy of 70.59%, reflecting the inherent difficulty of text‑based subtype differentiation. Conclusion The RAG‑LLM demonstrated excellent performance in binary classification of AO/OTA 31A versus 31B proximal femoral fractures using real‑world radiology reports. The systematic bias found in 31C labeling within MIMIC‑IV highlights the critical importance of expert data quality assurance in real‑world evidence studies. The comparable performance between zero‑shot and RAG models suggests that modern LLMs already possess inherent knowledge of AO/OTA classification, though RAG may offer advantages in more nuanced tasks. These findings support the potential of LLM‑assisted workflows to streamline fracture classification in clinical and research settings.

title: Giant Partially Thrombosed Ophthalmic Segment Internal Carotid Artery Aneurysm With Severe Angiographic–Radiological Discordance: Implications for Microsurgical Strategy
abstract: Abstract Background Giant partially thrombosed aneurysms of the ophthalmic segment of the internal carotid artery (ICA) present substantial diagnostic and therapeutic challenges because intraluminal thrombus and mural calcification can obscure the true aneurysm morphology, leading to underestimation of lesion size on angiography. Methods A 53-year-old man with progressive headache without focal neurological deficits or objective visual impairment underwent multimodal imaging including CT, MRI, CTA, and DSA. The imaging findings were integrated for operative planning, and microsurgical clipping with staged thrombectomy was performed. Results CT and MRI revealed a giant partially thrombosed ophthalmic segment ICA aneurysm compressing the optic apparatus, whereas DSA depicted only a small residual lumen, demonstrating marked angiographic–radiological discordance. Microsurgical clip reconstruction with staged intraluminal thrombectomy achieved complete aneurysm exclusion with preservation of the parent ICA and ophthalmic artery. The patient recovered without new neurological deficits and remained functionally independent at 6-month follow-up. Conclusions Giant partially thrombosed ophthalmic segment ICA aneurysms may be substantially underestimated by DSA alone. Integration of CT, MRI, CTA, and DSA is critical for defining true aneurysm morphology and optimizing skull base microsurgical strategy. Microsurgical reconstruction with staged thrombectomy remains a definitive treatment option in selected patients.

title: MOM-PD: Multimodal Biomarker Optimization for Parkinson's Disease Machine learning-assisted multimodal detection and clinical staging
abstract: Abstract Background: Parkinson's disease (PD) diagnosis relies primarily on clinical motor examination, and the prodromal phase preceding overt motor manifestations remains difficult to identify. No single biomarker modality has been shown to be both sensitive and specific across the full disease spectrum, and how best to integrate multimodal data for stage-specific detection is unclear. Objective: To optimize a multimodal biomarker framework using machine learning based on Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) data, and to define stage-specific biomarkerpanels for manifest PD detection, prodromal identification, and longitudinal progression monitoring. Methods: We analyzed 948 PPMI participants (445 PD, 389 prodromal, 111 healthy controls [HC], 3 SWEDD) with 18 candidate biomarkers spanning dopamine transporter SPECT (DaTscanSBR), structural MRI (FreeSurfer 7 cortical and subcortical metrics), diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and MDS-UPDRS Parts I–IV. Feature-wide association analysis with Mann-Whitney U tests and Cohen's d was followed by random forest Gini importance ranking. Random forest classifiers (500 trees, 5-fold stratified cross-validation) were trained on three feature sets: (1) DaTscan + clinical; (2) structural MRI only; (3) full multimodal combination. Four-year longitudinal trajectories (BL, V06, V10) of motor scores and grey matter volume were characterized. Results: For PD vs HC, the DaTscan-clinical model achieved near-perfect discrimination (AUC = 0.999, 95% CI 0.997–1.000), far exceeding structural MRI alone (AUC = 0.526). Top discriminative features were putaminal SBR, striatal SBR, and MDS-UPDRS Part III motor score. Prodromal vs HC discrimination was more challenging (AUC = 0.700), with subcortical grey matteratrophy as the leading signal while DaTscan SBR was non-discriminative (P = 0.43). PD vs prodromal classification was excellent (AUC = 0.984). Longitudinally, PD motor scores increased ~1.5 points/year and grey matter volume declined ~0.85%/year. Conclusions: Multimodal biomarkers display staging-dependent complementarity: DaTscan and motor scales dominate manifest PD identification, while subcortical volumetric MRI enablesprodromal detection. Stage-tailored biomarker panels support improved PD phenotyping and early screening for clinical trial enrichment.

title: Guidewire coating embolization to the pulmonary artery induced by puncture needle shear injury during cardiac radiofrequency ablation: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Hydrophilic-coated guidewires are essential tools in cardiac interventional procedures. Shear-induced detachment of the hydrophilic coating by a puncture needle represents a rare but potentially serious iatrogenic complication, as dislodged polymer fragments may embolize distally, leading to thrombosis, inflammatory responses, or pulmonary embolism. We present a case of hydrophilic guidewire coating embolization to the pulmonary artery resulting from shear injury by a puncture needle during radiofrequency catheter ablation for a left-sided accessory pathway. Case presentation: A 52-year-old woman with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome underwent radiofrequency catheter ablation. During the procedure, the hydrophilic coating of a guidewire was mechanically stripped by an 18-gauge beveled puncture needle. Fluoroscopy raised suspicion of an intravascular foreign body, and intraoperative cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) precisely localized two thin, loop-like coating fragments, approximately 6 cm and 3 cm in length, within branches of the right inferior pulmonary artery. The three-dimensional spatial information provided by CBCT directly guided the subsequent percutaneous snare retrieval. Both fragments were successfully retrieved via a minimally invasive percutaneous approach using a goose-neck snare. The patient remained asymptomatic throughout the hospital course, with no procedure-related complications, and was discharged on postoperative day 4. At 3-month follow-up, she continued to be symptom-free. Conclusion Percutaneous snare retrieval is an effective intervention for managing hydrophilic guidewire coating embolization to the pulmonary artery. Increased awareness of this complication, avoidance of withdrawing coated guidewires through metallic needles, routine inspection of device integrity, and intraoperative fluoroscopic monitoring are key preventive strategies.

title: Prediction of Lymph Node Metastasis Risk in Endometrial Cancer Using Multi-Sequence Magnetic Resonance Imaging Combined with Deep Transfer Learning
abstract: Abstract Purpose: To develop and externally validate a nomogram integrating clinical predictors, multisequence magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics, and deep learning (DL) features for preoperative lymph node metastasis (LNM) prediction in endometrial cancer (EC), and assess the incremental value of DL. Methods: This two-center retrospective study included 520 patients: 268 for training, 117 for held-out internal validation, and 135 for external validation. Radiomics features were extracted from four MRI sequences, and DL features from four ImageNet-pretrained 50-layer residual network (ResNet-50) branches fine-tuned in training. The Clinical+Radiomics model combined four clinical predictors with a radiomics signature; the nomogram additionally incorporated the DL signature. Final models were fitted using all training patients and evaluated unchanged in both validation cohorts. Assessments included DeLong tests, calibration, decision curve analysis, and prespecified sensitivity analysis in magnetic resonance (MR) report-based LNM-negative patients. Results: In internal and external validation, respectively, the nomogram achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.866 and 0.886, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of 0.786–0.946 and 0.817–0.955. Corresponding Clinical+Radiomics AUCs were 0.733 (95% CI: 0.591–0.875) and 0.715 (95% CI: 0.594–0.836), favoring the nomogram ( P =0.024 and P <0.001, respectively). Brier scores were 0.110 and 0.083. Decision curves favored the nomogram over comparators at probability thresholds of 0.02–0.39 and 0.01–0.71, respectively. Nomogram AUCs in MR report-based LNM-negative subgroups were 0.843 and 0.858, respectively. Conclusion: Adding DL improved discrimination beyond Clinical+Radiomics. The nomogram may complement preoperative LNM risk stratification but should not replace pathological nodal staging. Prospective multicenter validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Molecular landscape of medullary nephrocalcinosis in children – a nationwide, prospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background This study aimed to investigate the genetic landscape and to identify predictors of a molecular diagnosis in pediatric nephrocalcinosis. Methods This prospective, nationwide cohort study enrolled 79 unrelated pediatric patients with ultrasound-based medullary nephrocalcinosis of unknown etiology. Genetic evaluation was conducted using whole-exome sequencing ( n = 75) or targeted (Sanger) sequencing ( n = 4). Only (likely)pathogenic variants were considered diagnostic. Results A molecular diagnosis of Mendelian disease (MD) was established in 16% of patients, which included infantile hypercalcemia type 1 ( CYP24A1 , n = 3) and type 2 ( SLC34A1 , n = 2), familial hypomagnesemia, hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis ( CLDN16 , n = 2; CLDN19 , n = 1), distal renal tubular acidosis ( ATP6V0A4 , n = 1; ATP6V1B1 , n = 1), Bartter syndrome type 2 ( KCNJ1 , n = 1) and type 3 ( CLCNKB , n = 1), and Dent disease type 1 ( CLCN5 , n = 1). Monoallelic (MA) variants, possibly predisposing to nephrocalcinosis, were found in 16% of patients, encompassing four genes, predominantly within the SLC34A1 and SLC34A3 (61%). In patients with MD, except for two patients with Bartter syndrome, typical phenotypes were observed, in contrast to carriers of MA variants, in whom the majority had subtle abnormalities. Clinical parameters, prematurity and family history for nephrocalcinosis/lithiasis were not associated with MD diagnoses. Conclusions This study clarifies the distinct genetic architecture of pediatric nephrocalcinosis. The data may possibly explain the etiology in approximately 30% of cases, when considering both MD and MA variants. Disease-specific phenotypes are associated with MD; however, the absence of typical features should not preclude a genetic diagnosis.

title: Histopathological Profile of Tobacco-Associated Oral Mucosal Lesions in Chronic Cigarette Smokers: A Five-Year Retrospective Study from a Tertiary Care Centre in Pakistan
abstract: Abstract Background Tobacco smoking has been recognised as one of the key risk factors associated with a wide spectrum of oral mucosal alterations, ranging from benign reactive changes and epithelial dysplasia to malignant oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). Hence, in a population with high tobacco exposure, histopathological assessment remains central to characterise and diagnose potentially malignant and malignant disorders. Objective To evaluate the histopathological profile of tobacco-induced oral mucosal lesions among chronic cigarette smokers and to determine the incidence and degree of epithelial dysplasia and other smoking-associated histological alterations. Methods A retrospective cross-sectional study was carried out in the Department of Histopathology, Ziauddin University Hospital, Karachi, Pakistan. Histopathologically verified oral mucosal biopsy specimens obtained from chronic cigarette smokers from January 2020 to January 2026 were analysed. Information regarding demographics, smoking status, and clinical and histopathological data was derived from archived records. Hematoxylin and eosin-stained microscopic sections were used to study epithelial and stromal changes; epithelial dysplasia was classified according to World Health Organisation criteria. SPSS version 26.0 was used to analyse the data. Results The study was based on 50 oral mucosal biopsy specimens. The study population showed male dominance, with a mean age of 51.79 ± 13.39 years. Buccal mucosa was the most commonly affected anatomical site, while moderately differentiated infiltrative OSCC was the prominent histopathological diagnosis detected in 12 cases (24%). 50% of dysplastic lesions were mild, whereas moderate and severe lesions each accounted for 25%. Conclusion Chronic smoking was linked with a broad range of histopathological alterations in the oral mucosa. A substantial number of cases showed epithelial dysplasia and invasive OSCC. For those with long term use of tobacco, early detection and timely biopsy with histopathological analysis are crucial to identify potential malignant lesions and assess their development. Study findings may help optimise screening and preventive strategies for tobacco-attributed oral cancer in susceptible populations.

title: 18F-FET-PET/MRI versus Standard MRI for Radiotherapy Planning in High-Grade Brain Glioma: A Pilot Study (FETSMaRT)
abstract: Abstract Purpose High-grade gliomas carry a poor prognosis, and MRI-based radiotherapy (RT) planning may inadequately capture metabolically active tumor infiltration. ¹⁸F-fluoroethyl-tyrosine (FET) PET provides superior tumor delineation, yet prospective North American evidence supporting integration with RT planning remains limited. Methods FETSMaRT enrolled 30 patients with WHO grade 3 or 4 high-grade glioma receiving post-operative RT. FET-PET/MRI was acquired before RT with the radiation oncologist blinded to PET, enabling retrospective quantification of discordance between MRI-based and FET-PET/MRI-derived gross tumor (GTV), clinical target (CTV), and planning target (PTV) volumes. In the glioblastoma subgroup (n = 23), Kaplan–Meier and Cox analyses related GTV and CTV discordance to time to progression. title: Application of 3D Ultrasound Imaging in School-based Screening for Scoliosis: A Prospective Cross-sectional Study
abstract: Abstract Purpose To investigate the feasibility and efficacy of 3D ultrasound imaging for large-scale school-based scoliosis screening Methods This cross-sectional study screened 9,128 students using a three-stage protocol: (1) Adams test with scoliometer (ATR > 5° as positive); (2) 3D ultrasound imaging with an ultrasound curvature angle (UCA) > 8° for referral and UCA ≥ 10°as the optimal diagnostic threshold via ROC analysis; and (3) whole-spine X-ray as the gold standard (Cobb angle ≥ 10°). Agreement between ultrasound and X-ray measurements was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis and Pearson correlation. Diagnostic performance was evaluated with confirmed scoliosis defined as a radiographic Cobb angle ≥ 10°. Results Among 132 positive initial screenings, 98 underwent ultrasound and 67 had confirmed scoliosis (screen-detected prevalence of 0.73%). Mean UCA was 12.53°±4.15° and Cobb angle was 13.55°±6.11°. Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of -1.02° (95% LoA − 7.46° to 5.42°), with strong Pearson correlation (r = 0.91, p < 0.001; R² = 0.82). Among the 98 referred students, using UCA ≥ 10° as the threshold against X-ray-confirmed Cobb angle ≥ 10°, sensitivity was 89.5%, specificity 58.1%, accuracy 79.6%, PPV 82.2%, and NPV 72.0%. Conclusions This large population-based study confirms that 3D ultrasound serves as a feasible, radiation-free intermediate triage tool for school scoliosis screening. Our three-stage protocol preserves high sensitivity while cutting X-ray referrals by 25.8%. This tiered workflow minimizes unnecessary radiation exposure and optimizes healthcare resource use; refinements to referral thresholds and operator training may lower false-positive rates.

title: The Role of Bronchoscopy pada Acute Lung Atelectasis Due to Airway Mucus Plugging: A Case report
abstract: Abstract Background: Acute lung atelectasis caused by airway mucus plugging is a potentially reversible cause of respiratory failure, particularly in postoperative and critically ill patients. Prompt recognition and timely intervention are essential to prevent prolonged hypoxemia, mechanical ventilation, and other serious complications. Flexible bronchoscopy is considered the gold standard for diagnosing and treating obstructive atelectasis by directly identifying and removing airway obstruction. Case Presentation: A 32-year-old man developed severe hypoxemia and complete right lung atelectasis on the second day following exploratory laparotomy for abdominal trauma. Despite chest tube insertion, invasive mechanical ventilation, and supportive management, oxygenation remained critically impaired. Bedside lung ultrasonography demonstrated extensive right lung collapse. Therapeutic flexible bronchoscopy revealed complete obstruction of the right upper lobe bronchus by a thick mucus plug, with additional retained secretions in the right bronchial tree. Bronchial toilet and suctioning successfully restored airway patency. Immediate post-procedure chest radiography demonstrated significant right lung re-expansion, while arterial oxygenation improved markedly, with PaO₂ increasing from 40 mmHg to 194 mmHg. The patient was subsequently weaned from mechanical ventilation, experienced progressive clinical recovery, and was discharged from the intensive care unit in stable condition. Conclusion: This case highlights that mucus plug-induced atelectasis should be considered in postoperative patients presenting with sudden hypoxemia and radiographic evidence of lung collapse. Early therapeutic flexible bronchoscopy provides both definitive diagnosis and effective treatment by restoring airway patency, promoting rapid lung re-expansion, improving oxygenation, facilitating ventilator weaning, and optimizing clinical outcomes when conservative management is unsuccessful.

title: Emphysematous Osteomyelitis of the Lumbar Spine Masked by a Urinary Tract Infection in a Diabetic Patient: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Emphysematous osteomyelitis (EO) is a rare and aggressive gas-forming bone infection, most commonly affecting diabetic or immunocompromised patients, with the vertebrae, pelvis, and femur being frequently involved sites. It is most often caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae or Escherichia coli via hematogenous spread, and because of its rarity, its diagnosis is frequently overlooked. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 50-year-old diabetic and hypertensive female who presented with dysuria and dull lower back pain, initially managed as a routine UTI with antibiotics and adjustment of her diabetic regimen. When her urinary symptoms failed to resolve, contrast-enhanced CT of the kidneys, ureters, and bladder incidentally revealed emphysematous osteomyelitis of the L3-L4 vertebrae, with urine culture growing Klebsiella species. Despite targeted intravenous antibiotic therapy (meropenem), her clinical response was poor, necessitating anterior corpectomy with cage reconstruction. Her postoperative course was complicated by severe pain and poorly controlled diabetes, and she subsequently died of cardiopulmonary arrest. Conclusion: This case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for emphysematous osteomyelitis in diabetic patients presenting with back pain, as delayed diagnosis in an immunocompromised host can culminate in a fatal outcome despite aggressive medical and surgical management.

title: Automated Brachial Plexus Localization in Ultrasound Using Lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Abstract Purpose: Accurate localization of the brachial plexus in ultrasound images is critical for regional anesthesia and perioperative care. Traditional manual interpretation is time-consuming and operator-dependent, while segmentation-based deep learning models, though precise, often demand substantial computational resources, limiting deployment in resource-constrained settings. This study evaluated lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures for automated classification of brachial plexus nerve location into four anatomical quadrants, balancing predictive performance with computational efficiency for point-of-care (POC) environments. Methods: B-mode ultrasound images from the Kaggle Ultrasound Nerve Segmentation dataset were transformed from segmentation masks into a five-class classification task. Three CNN backbones—ResNet34, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNetB0—were trained using 3-fold cross-validation. Data augmentation and class-balancing strategies were applied. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrices, and pairwise statistical testing. Results All three models achieved comparable overall performance, with mean accuracies ranging from 0.7288 to 0.7320 and macro-averaged F1-scores from 0.7333 to 0.7365. ResNet34 had the highest mean accuracy and F1-score, though differences between architectures were not statistically significant. Per-class analysis revealed strong performance for majority classes (0 and 2) and lower precision and F1-scores for minority classes, particularly class 3. MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetB0 demonstrated high computational efficiency suitable for on-device deployment. Conclusion Lightweight CNN backbones provide reliable performance for brachial plexus quadrant classification in ultrasound images. While ResNet34 offered marginally higher accuracy, MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetB0 provided better suitability for POC deployment due to lower computational requirements. Future work should address class imbalance and expand evaluation to larger, more diverse datasets.

title: A tunable Synthetic Vascularized Eye Fundus for patient-free retinal imaging validation
abstract: Abstract The validation of novel retinal imaging techniques and motion-correction algorithms is often constrained by biological variability and the lack of ground-truth data in \textit{in vivo} measurements. To address this limitation, patient-free validation platforms require standardized targets that mimic selected optical and structural properties of the human eye. Here, we present a Synthetic Vascularized Eye Fundus (SVEF), a perfusable and contrast-tunable microfluidic insert designed for ophthalmic eye phantom platforms. The SVEF features a high-density, retinal-like vascular network fabricated by soft lithography using a custom polydimethylsiloxane-zinc oxide (PDMS--ZnO) composite. This substrate acts as a bright, diffusely scattering background, while perfusion with hemoglobin solutions generates physiologically relevant absorbing vessel-like structures. By optimizing the hemoglobin concentration, we achieved a vessel-to-background contrast closely matching that of \textit{in vivo} human fundus images. We validated the SVEF as a robust structural reference for image registration, demonstrating accurate retrieval of imposed saccade-like micro-displacements and enabling the enhancement of multi-frame fluorescence imaging. Finally, we confirmed the compatibility of the device with biological assays by successfully integrating and imaging human iPSC-derived retinal neurons. The SVEF provides a reproducible, patient-free environment for benchmarking ophthalmoscopic systems, optimizing image-registration pipelines and supporting versatile \textit{in vitro} retinal experiments.

title: Myxoid Onychomatricoma with Unusual CD99 Expression: A Report of a Rare Case and Literature Review.
abstract: Onychomatricoma (OM) is a rare, benign fibroepithelial tumor originating from the nail matrix, with different clinical and histological variants documented in existing studies. Myxoid OM is an even rarer subtype, characterized by a prominent fibromyxoid component in histopathology. We report a case of a 34-year-old male patient presenting with clinical manifestations consistent with typical OM. Histopathological examination revealed a biphasic tumor composed of an epithelial component and a prominent myxoid stroma, suggesting a diagnosis of myxoid OM. Notably, the tumor exhibited diffuse CD99 positivity, an extremely rare finding in OM. Histopathologically, myxoid OM shows considerable morphological overlap with superficial acral fibromyxoma (SAFM). Our case illustrates that CD99 positivity cannot serve as an absolute criterion to exclude OM; cautious interpretation of this marker is required to avoid diagnostic pitfalls in the differential diagnosis of these two entities. This case expands the immunophenotypic spectrum of myxoid OM and offers a valuable reference for its differential diagnosis. Furthermore, we include and provide a descriptive review to summarize the clinicopathological features and key differential diagnostic considerations of OM, with a focus on diagnostic pitfalls arising from rare histological variants and atypical immunophenotypes, to facilitate accurate differential diagnosis of subungual tumors.

title: Male Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Rare Case of Multisystem Involvement.
abstract: Background Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic autoimmune disease with diverse clinical manifestations. Although SLE predominantly affects women, male patients may present atypically, leading to diagnostic challenges and delays in treatment. Neuropsychiatric involvement and lupus nephritis represent severe manifestations associated with increased morbidity. Case presentation A 31-year-old man presented with fatigue, joint pain, fever, and a photosensitive skin rash. Laboratory investigations showed positive antinuclear antibodies and elevated anti-double-stranded DNA levels. Brain MRI demonstrated scattered T2-weighted and FLAIR hyperintensities suggestive of central nervous system vasculitis, while renal biopsy confirmed class IV lupus nephritis. The patient was treated with corticosteroids, hydroxychloroquine, and mycophenolate mofetil. Follow-up MRI and MRA performed after three weeks showed partial resolution of white matter lesions with stable vasculature. Clinical symptoms improved, and renal function stabilised. Conclusion This case highlights the importance of considering neuropsychiatric SLE in male patients presenting with neurological symptoms and multisystem involvement. MRI and MRA can play an important role in detecting central nervous system involvement and monitoring treatment response, while early recognition and prompt treatment may help prevent irreversible neurological complications.
